text.p: On overnight commodity markets, copper prices firmed in London on a small drawdown in stocks, while aluminium prices also rose on a stocks drawdown.
Wheat futures prices rose in Chicago on news Pakistan would buy 450,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, rather than Australian wheat.
Gold prices were mixed, but looked technically firmer in New York. Oil gained on short-covering and reports of possible conflict between Iran and Iraqi-based rebels.
The CRB index ended down 0.20 in New York at 239.31.
The widening spreads, along with a small drawdown in stocks provided support for copper.
Aluminium, helped by a 5,050-tonne decline in stocks, ended at its highs and $14 firmer at $1,584 per tonne.
Nickel finished sharply lower at $7,665, down $85. An attempt to bounce from its lows failed and prices resumed drifting lower.
Zinc was slightly easier at $1,213, down $6.50, following a stocks rise of 1,125 tonnes.

Copper prices ended modestly firmer in uninspired trading on Tuesday afternoon, joined by most of the other London Metal Exchange (LME) base metals. Widening backwardation in the copper market was the main feature in otherwise thin, quiet trading, traders said.
Three months delivery copper ended the kerb at $2,286 per tonne, up a modest $8 from Monday's kerb close.
But the cash to threes backwardation flared out after starting at around $60 in the morning, and ended the kerb at $72/$82.
CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on news Pakistan bought 450,000 tonnes of wheat from the U.S. and on a fund-generated surge to near limit gains in the corn pit, traders said.
There had been speculation late last week that Pakistan would purchase the wheat from the U.S. rather than from Australia because Australia is booked up for the near term.
The talk was confirmed on Monday when a Pakistan Food and Agriculture Ministry official announced the purchase.
Traders also said wheat was oversold and due for a bounce with evidence last week of a large number of fund shorts in wheat adding credence to that scenario.
Wheat closed two to 5-3/4 cents per bushel higher, with March up 4-3/4 at $3.64-1/4.
New York precious metals ended mixed in fairly light volume but gold and silver's technical health looked slightly better despite producer selling paring gains in the yellow metal, traders said.
Greg Drury of Mitsui and Co said producer selling of gold above the market was still a concern.
"Producers continue to be seriously underhedged," Drury said.
April COMEX gold settled $1.00 firmer at $347.70 an ounce, traded $348.80 to $346.10.
Bullion was quoted by dealers at $345.60 to $346.10.
NYMEX crude gained Tuesday afternoon on short covering, reversing early losses after weak heating oil fundamentals triggered a morning sell-off, traders said.
Some dealers said reports of clashes between security forces in central Iran and Iraq-based rebels came to the fore after selling in heat eased.
"We have had some short covering crude, but I can't help but think the Iran-Iraq headlines are in the back of peoples' minds," said a New York trader.
March crude was up 15 cents at $22.56 a barrel in late trade.

Crude fell as much as 52 cents to $21.89 Tuesday morning. State-run Tehran radio in Iran said on Monday that security forces killed three members of the Mujahideen Khalq opposition group and arrested a fourth.
Tehran has said the members come from neighbouring Iraq.
